what_it_measured.text: Safety endpoints and assessments The primary objective was to investigate the safety and tolerability of a single s.c. dose of PYY1875 as monotherapy and in combination with a single s.c. dose of 0.25-mg semaglutide in participants with overweight or obesity.

dose.text: In the first experiment, the animals were dosed once daily with 3, 30, or 100 nmol/kg of semaglutide or vehicle, s.c., for 4 weeks (n = 9 each).

route.text: In the first experiment, the animals were dosed once daily with 3, 30, or 100 nmol/kg of semaglutide or vehicle, s.c., for 4 weeks (n = 9 each).
(A) Change in body weight during daily s.c. doses of semaglutide (3, 30, or 100 nmol/kg) or vehicle.

endpoint.text: The primary endpoint was the number of treatment emergent adverse events (TEAEs) from day 1 to follow-up at day 36.
The primary endpoint in part 1 was the number of TEAEs from dosing (day 1) to EOS (week 24).

RESULTS Preclinical studies in DIO rats Diet-induced obese (DIO) rats that were treated with 3-, 30-, or 100- nmol/kg daily doses of s.c. semaglutide showed a mean (SD) of 8.8% (2.9%), 14.2% (3.0%), or 17.4% (5.7%) body weight loss, respectively, after 26 days of treatment, whereas vehicle-treated rats gained 4.8% (2.8%) body weight (Figure 1A).

A modest treatment difference of 2.2 percentage points (95% CI: 4.2 to 0.1) or 2.2 kg (95% CI: 4.1 to 0.3) was found for PYY1875 1.0 mg versus placebo as an add-on to TABL E 3 (Continued) PYY1875 1.0 mg, semaglutide 2.4 mg PYY1875 2.0 mg, semaglutide 2.4 mg Placebo, semaglutide 2.4 mg Total Infections and infestations 1 (12.5) 1 3 (37.5) 3 0 4 (16.7) 4 Skin and s.c. tissue disorders 1 (12.5) 1 1 (12.5) 1 2 (25.0) 2 4 (16.7) 4 Psychiatric disorders 1 (12.5) 2 1 (12.5) 1 1 (12.5) 1 3 (12.5) 4 Note: Data are expressed as n (%) E, where n is the number of participants reporting an event, % is the percentage of participants reporting an event, and E is the number of events.
PD findings PD endpoints were only assessed in part 2b and only in PYY1875- 1.0 + semaglutide versus placebo + semaglutide.
In part 2b (Figure 4B), a higher geometric mean plasma concentration of PYY1875 was observed with PYY1875-2.0 + semaglutide compared with PYY1875-1.0 + semaglutide.
Mean HbA1c decreased in a similar manner in the PYY1875-1.0 + semaglutide group and the placebo + semaglutide group (Figure 4F) during treatment and returned to baseline levels by EOS.
